The contract supports the replacement of existing equipment with modern, energy-efficient alternatives, contributing to improved operational performance, enhanced safety, reduced downtime, and YPO's sustainability objectives.
The procurement is divided into two lots:
Lot 1 - Warehouse Fleet: Provision and full-service support of a warehouse MHE fleet comprising reach trucks, counterbalance trucks, low-level order pickers (LLOPs) and powered pallet trucks (PPTs). The contract includes a real-time fleet management solution providing operational visibility, maintenance planning, fault diagnostics and performance reporting. The initial contract term is seven (7) years.
Lot 2 - Vehicle-Mounted Delivery Equipment: Provision and support of vehicle-mounted powered pallet trucks used within YPO's delivery operations. The initial contract term is three (3) years.
The contract includes all associated equipment, maintenance, labour, parts, training, support services and technologies required to maintain a safe, reliable and efficient fleet throughout the contract term.

tender.procurementMethodRationale:
This Direct Award is justified under Schedule 5, Paragraph 6(a) of the Procurement Act 2023, as the requirement can currently only be fulfilled using a specific component incorporated within an approved design and the absence of competition is attributable to technical reasons.
The approved container design incorporates a specific filter manufactured by Pall Europe Ltd. The component is required to maintain conformity with the approved design basis and associated engineering substantiation.
Pall Europe Ltd has advised that continued availability of the component cannot be guaranteed due to ongoing product portfolio rationalisation. Failure to secure sufficient stock whilst the component remains available would introduce a risk to continuity of supply for an operationally critical product.
Although alternative products may exist, adoption of an alternative component would require engineering assessment, testing, substantiation and approval activities to demonstrate continued compliance with the requirements of the approved design before implementation. These activities are expected to require a significant period to complete and cannot be concluded before continuity of supply risks materialise.
The proposed procurement therefore represents the most proportionate means of mitigating a known sole-source supply risk while maintaining compliance with the approved design and allowing sufficient time for the evaluation, qualification and implementation of any future alternative solution.
Accordingly, Sellafield considers that the conditions set out in Schedule 5, Paragraph 6(a) of the Procurement Act 2023 are satisfied and that a Direct Award to Pall Europe Ltd is justified.

Tendring District Council (TDC), Castle Point Borough Council (CPBC) and Braintree District Council (BDC), (the Authorities), are seeking to engage with the market and obtain expressions of interest ahead of a procurement for Temporary Accommodation of various types (at PME stage we are considering Supported and Unsupported Accommodation, including Block Bookings, PSL and Hotels/B&B, but the final  scope will be set out in more detail in the Tender notice).
One of the routes the Authorities are exploring is a 1- stage Open Tender Process with a view to establish a flexible framework under the Light Touch Regime - Section 9 of the Act, (for clarity, not an Open Framework as defined under the Procurement Act 2023).  
We anticipate the framework would be reopen periodically to allow new providers to apply for admission  to ensure the framework continues to support the Authorities in meeting their statutory duties-specifically, to maintain sufficient capacity in terms of available placements and provider coverage. 
Initially, the framework is likely to consist of 3 Lots (one per Authority above), but EPP reserves the right to create additional geographical Lots or categories during framework reopening/refresh periods. 
This PME exercise is intended to:
•	Engage with the market to gather insights and feedback on the proposed approach, and option development to support future decision-making.
•	Understand supplier capabilities, innovations, and potential delivery models.
•	Inform the development of a specification and procurement strategy that reflects market conditions and best practice.
This exercise does not commit the Authorities to any future model, contract value, contract duration or procurement route.

tender.title: National Vascular Registry
tender.description:
The National Vascular Registry (NVR) will be for NHS-funded vascular surgery and is expected to include several significant changes in scope compared to the existing specification (which runs to 31/12/2027 and is available on request using the registration link).  
 The initial contract is anticipated to be for a period of 3 years, with an indicative a maximum total budget for England only (see below regarding devolved nations) as follows: up to £1,619,337 excluding VAT  and £1,943,204.including VAT.  
Bids exceeding the maximum total budget will be rejected. It is currently expected that the extension value will be a 2 year pro rata of the core 3 year funding, estimated at £1,079,558 excluding VAT (England only).  
The figures stated here are based on the scope including England only. Other devolved nations could be included (particularly Wales) but details have not been finalised. The maximum contract value would be adjusted if additional areas are included. There is also potential to include aspirational intent measures (which will be defined in the service specification). 
 All values stated may be subject to change and the final values will be given when the tender goes live. 
 SCOPE OF THE AUDIT 
The role of a national clinical audit is to stimulate healthcare quality improvement through the provision of high-quality information on the organisation, delivery and outcomes of healthcare, together with tools and support to enable healthcare providers and other audiences to make best use of this information. Outcomes are benchmarked against national guidance and standards e.g. quality standards from the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE), and those from other established professional and patient sources. Successful national audits are those where the individuals providing the data can also improve the system, and there is a shared understanding of what good care looks like.  
 The National Vascular Registry was established in 2013 and currently collects information on five vascular surgical procedures: 
Repair of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) 
Carotid endarterectomy 
Lower limb angioplasty 
Lower limb bypass 
Lower limb amputation 
Since 2020 the NVR has collected device data for certain procedure types – the contractual arrangements for this have changed over time, and HQIP and funders are considering whether this should form part of the current contract opportunity. 
The overarching aim of this audit is to stimulate improvements in care for patients undergoing vascular surgery through the provision of high-quality comparative data from all providers of these services by measuring and reporting variations in quality of care and patient outcomes.  
For all HQIP-commissioned national clinical audits, the default expectation is that existing, routinely collected digital data will be used wherever available, and bespoke collection of data is avoided unless there is no other means of sourcing the data capable of meeting the needs of the project. Potential sources of existing digital data can include national data collections (for example, Hospital Episode Statistics and the Patient Episode Database for Wales), and Electronic Patient Records (EPR) data (whether from the system providers or via local data extraction and upload). Data is most useful locally for healthcare improvement when its provision to clinical teams is timely, the data is refreshed regularly and appropriate tools, support and guidance accompany the data outputs. The intent is for all of these features of the audit to be implemented and improved during the period of this contract. 
 This audit programme is expected to:  
a)Develop a robust, high-quality audit designed around key quality indicators likely to best support local and national quality improvement;  
b)Achieve, articulate and maintain close alignment with relevant NICE national guidance and quality standards throughout the audit, as appropriate;  
c)Enable improvements through the provision of timely, high-quality data that compares providers of healthcare, and comprises an integrated mixture of named trust, health board, commissioner, MDT, possibly consultant or clinical team level and other levels of reporting;  
dEngage parents, carers and families in a meaningful way, achieving a strong patient voice which informs and contributes to the design, functioning, outputs and direction of the audit;  
e)Consider the value and feasibility of additional data linkage, at an individual patient level, to other relevant national datasets either from the outset or in the future, and plan for these linkages from the inception of the contract;  
f)Ensure robust methodological and statistical input at all stages of the audit;  
g)Identify from the outset the full range of audiences for the results and other audit outputs, and plan and tailor them accordingly;  
h)Provide audit results in a timely, accessible and meaningful manner to support quality improvements, minimising the reporting delay and providing continual access to each unit for their own data;  
i)Utilise strong and effective project and programme management to deliver audit outputs on time and within budget; and   
j)Develop and maintain strong engagement with local clinicians, networks, commissioners, patients and their families and carers and charity and community support groups in order to drive improvements in services.

Real-Time Location System (RTLS)
Preliminary Market Engagement Notice
Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust (LTHT) intends to undertake a Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) exercise in relation to a potential requirement for a Real-Time Location System (RTLS).
Purpose of the Market Engagement
The purpose of this Preliminary Market Engagement is to:
• provide interested suppliers with an overview of the Trust's high-level requirements;
• understand the solutions, technologies and capabilities currently available in the market;
• obtain supplier feedback and market insight to help inform the Trust's requirements; and
• support the Trust in considering its potential future procurement strategy and approach.
The Trust is interested in engaging with suppliers that provide Real-Time Location System (RTLS) solutions, sometimes referred to as Real-Time Tracking Systems.
RTLS technology can be used to automatically identify and track the location of assets, equipment, inventory and, where appropriate, people in real time. Through this engagement, the Trust wishes to develop its understanding of available solutions and how these may support its operational requirements.
Supplier Market Engagement Webinar
As part of the Preliminary Market Engagement exercise, the Trust intends to hold a virtual supplier engagement webinar as follows:
Date: Wednesday, 11 November 2026
Time: 1:00 pm to 3:00 pm
Location: Microsoft Teams
Suppliers wishing to participate should email the Trust and provide:
• the name of their organisation;
• the names of up to two (2) representatives who will attend; and
• the email address of each nominated representative.
Following registration, the Microsoft Teams invitation will be issued directly to the nominated representatives.
About Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust
Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust is one of the largest and busiest acute hospital trusts in the UK. The Trust has a budget of approximately £1.7 billion, employs more than 25,000 staff, and treated more than 1.7 million patients last year.
The Trust's hospital sites include:
• Leeds General Infirmary (LGI), including Leeds Children's Hospital and Leeds Dental Institute;
• St James's University Hospital (SJUH), including Leeds Cancer Centre;
• Seacroft Hospital;
• Wharfedale Hospital; and
• Chapel Allerton Hospital.
Important Information
This notice relates to Preliminary Market Engagement only and does not constitute the commencement of a formal procurement or competitive tendering process.
Participation or non-participation in this market engagement will not, in itself, confer any advantage or disadvantage on any supplier in relation to any potential future procurement exercise.
The Trust is not committed to commencing a procurement process following this engagement. Any future procurement opportunity will be subject to the Trust's governance requirements and the applicable procurement rules.
In addition, you can e-mail your representatives e-mail to d.acheampong@nhs.net if interested in the preliminary market engagement webinar.

criteria.description:
F&HDC will evaluate your RTP in the following order:
i.	Validation of your RTP submission to confirm it has been completed correctly and in accordance with the instructions.
ii. Determination of whether your organisation is an 'excluded' or 'excludable' supplier (RTP Response document Sections 1 and 2).
ii.	Financial risk assessment.
iii.	Technical question evaluation in accordance with the marking criteria.
The maximum quality score of 100% is divided across each of the quality questions in RTP Supplier Response document Section 3. The weighting of each question is shown below.
•	Q1: RELEVANT EXPERIENCE 30 %
•	Q2: PROGRAMME 20 %
•	Q3: TECHNICAL METHODOLOGY 20 %
•	Q4: DESIGN MANAGEMENT 20 %
•	Q5: HEALTH & SAFETY 10 %
•	Total Quality Score 100 %
Once we have scored all the 'quality' questions in Section 3.1, we will rank the RTPs by this score using 'standard competition ranking' (e.g. 12245). We expect to select five organisations for the second stage.
However, if the scores of some applicants are the same or very close, we might choose to invite more than five organisations to tender. For example: if the rankings are 1 2 3 4 5 5, where two organisations are both ranked 5 with the same score, we will invite both those organisations.
Similarly, if the rankings are 1 2 3 3 5 6, we could invite the organisation ranked 6th, if their score is very similar to organisation 5. However, this would be at F&HDC's discretion.

tender.title: Direct Award of Property and Development Agreements for the Royal Bolton Hospital Retail Development Scheme.
tender.description:
Bolton NHS Foundation Trust ("BFT") has entered into a Ground Lease dated 11 September 2026 with Noviniti Dev Co 14 Ltd ("Noviniti") ("Ground Lease") in respect of land at Royal Bolton Hospital, Minerva Road, Farnworth, Bolton ("the Hospital") which has been identified by Noviniti as the site of a proposed building extension to the existing entrance to the Hospital. The development will accommodate 3 new retail units and associated office and storage plus circulation space within the building extension plus 3 further retail units and internal refurbishment works within the existing Hospital building and minor external works ("the Potential Development"). 
The agreement leading to the grant of the Ground Lease was the subject of (inter alia) a Transparency Notice published on 16 June 2026 reference 2026/5-000-056489, a Contract Award Notice published on 26 June 2026 reference 2026/5-000-060495 and a Contract Details Notice published on 7 September 2026 reference 2026/S 000-084619.  
The Ground Lease is for a term of 35 years, subject to earlier break rights in favour of BFT at the expiry of two years from the date of grant of the Ground Lease (exercisable in the event that the works to undertake the Potential Development have not been commenced by that date) and again as an absolute right on the date 30 years from the date of completion of the Potential Development. 
BFT now intends (subject to receiving business case sign off from the Trust Board) to enter into further documentation relating to the Potential Development being:- 
(a)	a Licence for Alterations under the Ground Lease authorising Noviniti to undertake the Potential Development;
(b)	a Deed of Variation of the Ground Lease varying the terms of the BFT break rights; and
(c)	a multi party Agreement for Lease ("S2AFL") with Noviniti, WH Smith Hospitals Ltd ("the Operator") and WH Smith Hospital Holdings Ltd ("the Guarantor") and BFT's wholly owned subsidiary Integrated Facilities Management Bolton Limited ("IFM").
IFM are referenced in this Notice as a potential party to the S2AFL and the other documents requiring to be executed (including the Licence for Alterations; the Deed of Variation of the Ground Lease; the Operator Lease and the Trust Retail Leases on the basis that it has a short term leasehold interest in relevant areas of the Hospital to accommodate its role as facilities manager on behalf of BFT.  On the basis that it is a wholly owned subsidiary of BFT, it is not considered necessary to separately advertise IFM's role and where IFM does not have relevant property interest requiring it to enter into the relevant leasehold documents, IFM will not be a party.
Under the S2AFL, Noviniti is not obliged to carry out the Potential Development but if it does not BFT may exercise its break rights to terminate the Ground Lease if Noviniti does not commence the relevant works by an agreed deadline. 
Under the terms of the S2AFL, if Noviniti completes the construction of the Potential Development, the Operator is obliged to accept a Lease of the completed building extension for use for retail purposes ("the Operator Lease"). The Operator Lease will be for a term of 15 years from completion of the Potential Development. 
Under the terms of the S2AFL, BFT are obliged to accept a Reversionary Lease of the completed building extension for a term of 15 years commencing on the term expiry date of the Operator Lease ("Reversionary Lease").
The S2AFL also provides for the grant to the Operator by BFT (and IFM where appropriate) of three occupational leases of areas within the existing Hospital entrance for retail purposes ("the Trust Retail Leases"). Two of the Trust Retail Leases will be for a term of 15 years co-terminus with the Operator Lease, the third will start later (approximately 26 January 2028) and will end on 28 March 2042 All the Trust Retail Leases will be terminable in the event of the Operator Lease being determined prior to lease expiry.
The S2AFL further provides that on completion of the Operator Lease, the Operator will grant to BFT a sub-lease of the structure of the building extension demised by the Operator Lease - giving BFT control of and responsibility for the structure and common parts of that building/extension ("Structure and Common Parts Lease"). 
The S2AFL contains provision for BFT to accept a direct lease of the building extension from Noviniti ("Step-in Lease") in the event that the Operator defaults and fails to enter into the Operator Lease when required to do so.  The Step-in Lease would be on substantially similar terms to the Operator Lease (including rent payment profile) and for a similar term of 15 years.  In the event that the Operator defaults during the term of the Operator Lease and the Operator Lease is determined, then BFT will be obliged to step into the position of the Operator and accept the grant of an "Overriding Lease" ("Overriding Lease").  The Overriding Lease would be on substantially similar terms as the Operator Lease (including rent payment profile) and be for a period from the date of default by the Operator to the date which would have been the term expiry date under the Operator Lease. 
The S2AFL contains provision for BFT and the Operator to enter into a Deed of Covenant for payment of monies by the Operator to BFT as calculated in the Deed of Covenant plus sums calculated by reference to turnover above specified thresholds in respect of the trading income from the retail units comprised in the Operator Lease.  The Deed of Covenant will contain provisions relating to reimbursement of sums to the Operator as tenant in scenarios where BFT is at fault or certain adverse events impacting trading income from the Retail Units in the Operator Lease take place.
The Potential Development involves construction of a new building extension within the area demised to Noviniti by the Ground Lease and also works to the existing Hospital entrance outside of the Ground Lease demise to create retail and ancillary space within that area and also minor works to the exterior.  The works within the demise of the Ground Lease account for approximately 90% of the total costs of the Potential Development. 
Under the terms of the S2AFL and the Licence for Alterations, Noviniti is under no obligation to serve notice to elect to carry out the Potential Development.  No public works contract arises due to the lack of an enforceable obligation to undertake the Potential Development. 
Following completion of the Ground Lease, Noviniti has control of part of the site of the Potential Development and has the exclusive right to the land on which various of the works comprised in the Potential Development are to be undertaken.  In practice, no other party can undertake the whole of the Potential Development without Noviniti's consent whilst the Ground Lease exists and remains in place ie until such time as the BFT break right under the Ground Lease becomes capable of exercise on 11 September 2028.  As such, the justification for direct award set out in Schedule 5, paragraph 5(a) of the Procurement Act 2023 ("PA2023") applies.  In addition, the arrangements constitute "an exempted contract" for the purposes of the PA2023 being contracts for the acquisition of interests or rights in respect of land or buildings and/or which concern interests or rights over land or buildings, in accordance with Schedule 2, Part 2, paragraph 8 of the PA2023.

tender.procurementMethodRationale:
As part of the UK’s nuclear decommissioning programme, Nuclear Restoration Services (NRS) will begin taking ownership of assets and the responsibility for the Advanced Gas-Cooled Reactor (AGR) sites from EDF Energy Nuclear Generation Limited (EDF) commencing on 1st April 2026 for Hunterston B followed by Hinkley B in October 2026 and marks a key milestone in ensuring the continued safe, secure and cost-effective decommissioning of the UK’s nuclear legacy.
NRS is committed to transparency and collaboration throughout this transfer process, working closely with EDF, regulators and stakeholders to deliver a seamless transfer whilst maintaining the highest standards of regulatory, safety and environmental compliance. In line with this commitment, NRS placed a direct award in accordance with Section 41 of the Procurement Act 2023 and wishes to advise that the EDF contract with Allen Fencing Ltd, as detailed in this notice, was being novated to Nuclear Restoration Services (NRS) as part of the AGR site transfer process. This is a direct award for the purposes of Procurement Act 2023 and is pursuant to Paragraph 6 of Schedule 5 to the Procurement Act 2023
NRS considered Paragraph 6 applies as the services provided by Allen Fencing Ltd are critical to the ongoing operation of Hinkley B and it would create significant technical difficulties and unacceptable regulatory risks to NRS for another supplier to supply the services at this time.
Following completion of this novated contract, all future requirements will be progressed through NRS’s established procurement processes and in continued compliance with the Procurement Act 2023 (PA23).
Allen Fencing is neither an excluded or excludable supplier.
** Please Note **
This is a framework and will be called off as and when required.

Support compliance with relevant health and safety legislation, including the Work at Height Regulations 2005, and ensure safe systems of work are implemented at all times.

Minimise disruption to patients, visitors and staff while ensuring services are delivered efficiently and in accordance with agreed schedules and specifications.
Obtain best value for money through a competitive procurement process that balances quality, safety, service delivery and cost effectiveness.
Appoint a contractor capable of delivering reliable contract management, trained and competent operatives, and continuous compliance with NHS policies, statutory requirements and environmental responsibilities.
Overall, the procurement seeks to establish a long-term partnership with a contractor that can deliver safe, compliant and high-quality window cleaning services, helping both Trusts maintain healthcare environments that are clean, welcoming and fit for patients, staff and visitors
